data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 proposes a 'shared mechanism' relation between SRC_003 and SRC_005, but the endpoints it describes do not share a mechanism — they share only an analogous risk surface. SRC_003's mechanism is a rubric-level declaration forbidding a homogenization mutation (no program assertion), while SRC_005's mechanism is a program-level mutation-and-assertion cycle. The target even concedes the difference is enforcement (rubric marking vs program assertion), which means the actual mechanism (the enforcement discipline by which the mutation is caught) differs. Calling this a shared mechanism conflates the attack vector (identity homogenization) with the mechanism (rubric declaration vs program assertion), and the target's own refutation condition — different comparison axes mean the mechanism is merely analogous — is substantively triggered since school-ID partial-key binding and endpoint-drift-field lease binding are distinct comparison axes.
